summary.text: 大 is a whole-graph picture of a standing adult human, commonly used for “big” or “great.” The proposed original sense “adult” and its development to “big” are an interpretation; early evidence also records 大 used opposite 小, but no dated sequence establishes that semantic transition.

formation.text: Pictographic: the complete graph is analyzed as a frontal human figure, not as a compound of smaller signs. Interpretations of the pose differ: some describe outstretched arms, while a specialist account describes arms hanging down; the available research did not inspect an individual ancient specimen to settle the details.

components.text: The whole graph 大 depicts a frontal standing adult human. This is a pictographic analysis, not a decomposition into separate components. Although some accounts describe outstretched arms, another describes them hanging down; the pose and proposed original sense remain interpretations.

history.text: Historical form accounts label forms as oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal and standard script, with the standard form described as close to small seal. The selected oracle, bronze and Shuowen seal images are modern redrawings in those styles. They support broad comparison, but not a detailed stroke-by-stroke path or a precise chronology of graphic changes.
The Shuowen dictionary says 大 depicts a human and records it as an ancient form of 亣. This is an important historical explanation, but it is not independent proof of prehistoric origin.

uncertainties.text: The outstretched-arms description conflicts with the specialist account of arms hanging down. No individual ancient specimen was retrieved and visually inspected here to resolve the pose.
The earliest precisely dated attestation of 大 meaning “adult” or “big” was not established. The reported bronze use meaning “big” is not independently dated here.

The proposed development from “adult” to “big” lacks an independently dated sequence of intermediate uses. Broad script-style labels also do not establish specific graphic changes, corruption, or variant chronology.

senses.text: A specialist analysis proposes “adult,” contrasted with child, as the original sense; no precisely dated attestation for this sense was established.

senses.period: bronze inscription reported; exact date unresolved
senses.text: A specialist account reports 大 used for “big,” opposite 小, in a bronze inscription. The specific vessel and date were not independently verified here.
“Great” is a current gloss for 大.

developments.text: A specialist account proposes that “big” developed from “adult,” but the intermediate semantic stages are not documented in a dated sequence.
Both senses are recorded, but the supplied evidence does not establish that “great” developed from “big” or provide a chronology linking them.

limitations.text: The proposed adult-to-big development is an interpretation, not a dated chain of attestations; the earliest precisely dated sense remains unresolved.
The supplied modern glosses do not establish a historical sequence among “big,” “great,” “vast,” “large,” and “high.”

overview.text: 大 is a picture of a standing adult human, used for “big” and “great.” A specialist account proposes “adult” as an earlier sense, but the surviving evidence here does not establish that transition in a dated sequence.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a standing adult figure; it is not built from smaller signs. The figure’s pose is interpreted differently across accounts.
